items.summary: The Supreme Court on Sunday asked Delhi authorities to explain why contempt of court action should not be initiated against them for closure of metro stations on October 10 amid the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests. A total of 45 metro stations, mostly in and around Central Delhi, were shut on October 10 in view of the protests at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The closure of metro stations along with detention of key CJP leaders and opposition members had led to a flurry of petitions before the Supreme Court. The principal matter before the Court was a contempt petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Chairperson D Thara. The plea alleged that Delhi Metro stations remained closed on Sunday despite the Supreme Court's October 9 saying there shouldn't be complete shutdown of public transport ahead of the protests. items.title: BREAKING: Prima facie contempt case made out over Delhi Metro restrictions during protests, says Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court has held that a prima facie case of contempt of court has been made out over the alleged violation of its October 9 directions concerning restrictions on Metro and railway services in Delhi during the October 10 protests. A Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana recorded the finding in its written order following a special Sunday hearing on a contempt petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi. The contempt plea was filed against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Chairperson D Thara. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana " Having considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the averments in the Contempt Petition, we are of the opinion that the petitioners have made out a prima facie case. Accordingly, we issue notice upon the alleged contemnors ," the Court said. The alleged contemnors have been directed to file counter-affidavits, along with a report on compliance with the Court's October 9 order, by October 13. items.title: Three killed as Mini Cooper rams scooter near Kochi airport
items.summary: Three people, including two 21-year-old women, were killed after a speeding Mini Cooper rammed into their scooter near Nedumbassery in Kerala’s Ernakulam district in the early hours of Sunday, October 11. Police have confirmed that the driver had consumed alcohol and are investigating whether he had used other intoxicating substances. The deceased have been identified as Ijaz, a native of Karnataka, Devika from Wayanad and Gopika from Palakkad. All three worked at a shop in Thrikkakara and were returning towards Athani after stopping for tea near the Cochin International Airport. View this post on Instagram The accident occurred around 1.45 am near Moozhiyal, close to Suvarnodyanam and the Athani signal, when the Mini Cooper allegedly hit their scooter from behind. The impact threw the three onto the road, causing severe injuries. The car reportedly dragged the scooter for nearly 100 metres before stopping. All three succumbed to their injuries. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.

items.title: Protesters want Bedti-Aghanashini project scrapped, seek conservation plan for Western Ghats rivers
items.summary: Hundreds of people gathered at Freedom Park on Saturday, October 11, to protest the proposed Bedti-Aghanashini river-linking project, urging the government to abandon the plan in the interest of the Western Ghats and Uttara Kannada district. Organised under the banner "Save Western Ghats, Protect Uttara Kannada" by the Bedti-Aghanashini Valley Conservation Committee, the protest drew people from Uttara Kannada living in Bengaluru. The gathering adopted 11 resolutions demanding the immediate scrapping of the proposed Bedti-Aghanashini river projects and suspension of the DPR process for the Bedti-Varada link. They also called for a sustainable conservation plan for the 22 major rivers originating in the Western Ghats and their basins. They also urged that the Bedti, Aghanashini and Shalmala valleys be protected, and that the government come up with non-destructive irrigation methods for farmers in Uttara Kannada district. items.title: A city under siege by its own guardians: The Delhi of October 9 and 10
items.summary: On October 9, as the sun gently set over central Delhi, the city fell into an unusually quiet lull. It was the day before the protests demanding the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar, the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and a rollback of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. If it weren’t so dystopian, it might have been called calm. The road leading to the protest site at Jantar Mantar had been barricaded at both ends. New surveillance cameras and loudspeakers were strapped to trees every few hundred metres. From the speakers, a woman’s voice, unhurried and polite, warned people not to join the next day’s demonstration. Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita was in force, she said. Gatherings of five or more, slogans, and protest symbols were prohibited. Then the message played again, and again, in a continuous loop. Closer to Jantar Mantar, a policeman stood over a labourer as he welded four rows of metal barricades into one, so that no protester could drag them apart. According to reports, the incident occurred at Connaught Place while John Brittas was speaking to the media. He stated that security personnel pinned him down and manhandled him inside a vehicle despite him identifying himself as an MP. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has stayed two FIRs registered against BJP Booth Level Agents accused of trying to delete voters' names from electoral rolls by filing bulk Form 7 objections during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the Malleswaram Assembly Constituency. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde granted the interim relief on two separate writ petitions filed by the agents on Saturday, October 10, LiveLaw reported . Form 7 is used to object to the inclusion of a name in the rolls or to seek deletion of an entry. The petitioners, GS Vasanthalakshmi and Deepak Singh R, sought the quashing of the FIRs registered at the Vyalikaval and Yeshwanthpura police stations in Bengaluru.
